answer: Each operator holds one host-attested mirror; its kth identity needs a new inlet etched k pigment layers deep, and etching destroys one pigment per layer. The mirror measures depth through the inlet, so layers cannot be poured in parallel or split across hosts. A fresh wallet must cut its inlet into the same mirror and starts at the existing layer count, not zero. The first identity costs one pigment, the tenth ten, the thousandth a thousand; an operator's bill is the sum of all inlet depths already on that mirror.
